title: Story Pitch: Craft & Convince
description: You are preparing for the Regional Storytelling Championship. Over 12 weeks, craft your narrative, develop a compelling brand voice, adapt to diverse audiences, overcome stage fright, and pitch your story to a panel of judges. Every decision shapes your story's power and your performance on stage.
how_to_play: You have 12 weeks to prepare for and compete in the Regional Storytelling Championship.
Each round presents a decision about crafting your story, honing your delivery, or managing your creative identity.
Watch your dashboard — Narrative Mastery, Audience Connection, Performance Skills, and Creative Identity are all interconnected.
Random events like surprise workshops, rival upsets, and audience feedback will test your adaptability.
NPCs (Coach Maya, Judge Stern, Rival Rai) react to your progress in real time.
Aim for balanced growth — a powerful story means nothing without stage presence, and charisma alone won't cover a weak narrative!
learning_objectives: Understand the elements of compelling storytelling: structure, emotion, and voice
Practice persuasive communication and adapting messages to different audiences
Develop confidence in public speaking and stage presence
Learn to take creative risks and build a personal brand voice
Build empathy by crafting stories that resonate with diverse listeners
cultural_context: Regional storytelling tradition, youth competitions, persuasive communication across cultures

tick_rules.label: Judge Awareness

interactions.label: Emotional Resonance
interactions.description: Deep emotional storytelling naturally draws the audience in.

interactions.label: Distinctive Voice
interactions.description: A strong personal voice makes every narrative more compelling.

interactions.label: Stage Command
interactions.description: High confidence translates into commanding stage presence.

interactions.label: Creative Complacency
interactions.description: Overconfidence without creative risk leads to a generic, predictable voice.

random_events.label: Surprise Masterclass

random_events.news_text: SPECIAL: Renowned storyteller visits — students get exclusive masterclass on narrative craft!
random_events.ai_image_prompt: Teenage students in a bright workshop room, famous storyteller at front gesturing dramatically, engaged audience, notebooks open, inspirational atmosphere

random_events.label: Viral Video
random_events.description: A practice session video of yours goes viral on social media! The attention is thrilling but also adds pressure.
random_events.news_text: Your practice video goes viral! 50K views overnight. Everyone's watching now...
random_events.ai_image_prompt: Teenage student looking at phone with thousands of likes and shares, mix of excitement and nervousness, school hallway background, semi-realistic

random_events.label: Harsh Critic Review
random_events.description: A guest critic gives your preliminary performance a brutal review. It stings, but there's truth in the feedback.
random_events.news_text: Tough love from the critics! Your narrative needs work, but the feedback is a gift in disguise.

behaviors.message: Your story structure needs work. Let's focus on the basics — a strong opening, rising tension, and a meaningful resolution.
Your narrative craft is really coming together! The judges will notice this level of sophistication.
You're making me feel things! That emotional authenticity is what separates good storytellers from great ones.
The competition is weeks away and you're underprepared! We need an intensive practice schedule immediately.
I've seen your preliminary work. Frankly, it lacks originality and polish. You'll need to step up significantly.
Now THAT is the kind of storytelling that wins championships. Keep this standard up.
Judge Stern announces that based on preliminary reviews, your entry may not qualify for the final round unless you show dramatic improvement!
Okay, I'll admit — your story is doing something different. I need to raise my game too.
Saw your rehearsal. You looked nervous up there. The judges eat timid storytellers alive, you know.
Rival Rai debuts an experimental storytelling format that goes viral. Your conventional approach suddenly feels outdated. You're stuck — creatively blocked!

news_templates.text: Narrative skill at {narrative_skill}! Your story structure is turning heads in practice rounds.
Buzz is building — people are calling you a natural performer!

simulation_config.ai_scene_prompt_template: A teenage storyteller preparing for a regional competition, confidence level {confidence}%, narrative skill {narrative_skill}%, creative risk {creative_risk}%. Rehearsal space with story notes on walls, stage lighting in background. Mood: {'electrifying' if confidence > 65 else 'anxious' if confidence < 35 else 'focused'}.

rounds.situation: The Regional Storytelling Championship is 12 weeks away. Coach Maya says the first step is finding your 'story seed' — the core idea that everything else grows from. You have several directions to explore.
rounds.goal: Choose the foundation for your competition story.
rounds.coaching_moment: Creativity: Great stories begin with a single, powerful idea. Choosing your seed wisely sets the trajectory for everything that follows.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What makes a story idea worth telling? How do you know which seed will grow into something powerful?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager sitting at desk brainstorming story ideas, notebooks and mind maps spread out, light bulb moment, warm study room, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. A Personal Experience
choices.description: Draw from a real moment in your life — authentic but requires vulnerability.
choices.feedback: Personal stories have raw power. Vulnerability is scary but deeply authentic.

skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.

choices.label: B. A Cultural Legend Retold
choices.description: Take a traditional folktale and give it a modern twist. Familiar but needs fresh perspective.
choices.feedback: Retelling legends lets you stand on the shoulders of centuries of storytelling tradition.

skill_explanation.creativity: Thinking outside the box leads to more original solutions.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.

choices.label: C. A Social Issue Story
choices.description: Craft a story around a real-world issue — powerful but risks being preachy.
choices.feedback: Stories about real issues can change minds — if you show rather than preach.

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.

choices.label: D. An Original Fantasy World
choices.description: Invent a completely new world and characters. High creative risk, high reward.
choices.feedback: Bold and original! Fantasy gives you total creative freedom, but you'll need to work harder to ground it emotionally.

skill_explanation.creativity: Exploring an unconventional approach shows creative thinking.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Evaluating risk vs. reward is a key life skill.

rounds.situation: Coach Maya says every championship story needs strong structure. She presents three structural frameworks used by top storytellers. The structure you choose will shape how your story flows and how the audience experiences it.
rounds.goal: Choose a narrative structure for your story.
rounds.coaching_moment: Strategic thinking: Structure is invisible to the audience but it's the backbone that holds everything together. Choose strategically.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why does the order and structure of a story matter as much as its content?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Whiteboard with story structure diagrams, three-act structure, hero's journey chart, teenager studying them with a mentor, classroom setting, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. Classic Three-Act Structure
choices.description: Beginning, middle, end. Reliable, proven, but can feel formulaic.
choices.feedback: The three-act structure has worked for thousands of years. Reliability is a superpower.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Prioritizing long-term gains over short-term comfort builds character.

choices.label: B. Non-Linear Timeline
choices.description: Start at the climax, then weave backwards. Gripping but technically demanding.
choices.feedback: Non-linear storytelling is bold! It demands precision but creates unforgettable moments.

skill_explanation.creativity: Looking at the problem from a new angle demonstrates creativity.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Taking a calculated risk shows you can handle uncertainty.

choices.label: C. Parallel Storylines
choices.description: Weave two stories that converge at the end. Complex but deeply satisfying.
choices.feedback: Parallel stories are a masterclass in craft. High complexity, but the payoff is extraordinary.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.
skill_explanation.creativity: Combining ideas in unexpected ways shows innovative thinking.

choices.label: D. Minimalist Single-Scene
choices.description: One scene, one moment, told with intense focus. Less is more.
choices.feedback: Minimalism demands bravery. Every word must earn its place. But simplicity can be devastating.

skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.

rounds.situation: Coach Maya says the judges look for a distinctive voice — the quality that makes YOU sound like nobody else. She's arranged different exercises to help you find yours.
rounds.coaching_moment: Creativity and brand voice: Your voice is your fingerprint as a storyteller. It's not just what you say, but how you say it.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What makes your way of telling a story different from anyone else's?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager performing in front of a mirror, practicing different vocal styles, expression exercises, bedroom with posters of storytellers, warm lighting

choices.label: A. Lean Into Humor
choices.description: Develop a witty, warm storytelling style. Audiences love to laugh — but humor is hard to master.
choices.feedback: Humor disarms audiences and makes them lean in. But the best humor also carries truth.

skill_explanation.creativity: Not settling for the obvious solution builds creative problem-solving.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.

choices.label: B. Poetic & Lyrical
choices.description: Focus on beautiful language, rhythm, and imagery. Enchanting but risks sounding pretentious.
choices.feedback: Poetic language creates magic. When every sentence sings, the audience is spellbound.

skill_explanation.creativity: Thinking outside the box leads to more original solutions.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Choosing a future benefit over an immediate reward shows patience.

choices.label: C. Conversational & Raw
choices.description: Talk to the audience like a friend. Natural, relatable, but needs strong stage presence to land.
choices.feedback: Conversational style makes you instantly relatable. Audiences feel like they know you.

skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.

choices.label: D. Theatrical & Dramatic
choices.description: Big gestures, dramatic pauses, multiple character voices. High impact, high energy.
choices.feedback: Theatrical storytelling is electrifying! The audience will never be bored, but it demands fearless energy.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.
skill_explanation.resilience: Facing challenges head-on strengthens your resilience over time.

rounds.situation: The championship has three rounds, each with a different audience: kids (ages 8-10), peers (ages 12-14), and adult judges. Coach Maya says you need to adapt your story for at least one test audience this week.
rounds.goal: Practice adapting your story for a specific audience.
rounds.coaching_moment: Adaptability: The same story told differently can inspire a child, move a peer, or impress a judge. Great communicators adapt without losing authenticity.
rounds.reflection_prompt: How does knowing your audience change the way you tell a story?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager presenting a story to three different groups shown in split screen: young children, peers, and adult judges, diverse school auditorium

choices.label: A. Practice with Young Kids
choices.description: Tell your story to a group of 8-year-olds. Their honest reactions will reveal if your story truly connects.
choices.feedback: Kids are the ultimate test — they have zero patience for boring stories. If they listen, you're onto something.

skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.

choices.label: B. Perform for Peer Group
choices.description: Present to classmates. They'll give real feedback, but peer pressure makes it nerve-wracking.
choices.feedback: Performing for peers is terrifying and essential. Their feedback is gold — even when it stings.

skill_explanation.resilience: Pushing through difficulty builds mental strength.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Not always playing it safe helps you grow as a decision-maker.

choices.label: C. Present to Teachers
choices.description: Get structured feedback from English and drama teachers. Formal and insightful.
choices.feedback: Teacher feedback is structured and expert. They see things peers miss — craft, structure, pacing.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Investing effort now for later payoff builds discipline.

choices.label: D. Record & Self-Review
choices.description: Film yourself and analyze the recording. Objective but you miss live audience energy.
choices.feedback: Watching yourself is uncomfortable but eye-opening. You see every nervous habit and missed beat.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.

rounds.situation: Coach Maya says your story has good structure but needs a stronger emotional core — the moment that makes the audience feel something real. She wants you to dig deeper this week.
rounds.goal: Strengthen the emotional heart of your story.
rounds.coaching_moment: Empathy: Stories that move people aren't just clever — they tap into universal human emotions. What does your story make people feel?
rounds.reflection_prompt: What is the one emotion you want your audience to carry with them after your story ends?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager deep in thought journaling in a quiet park, autumn leaves, emotional expression, writing in a notebook, reflective mood, golden hour light

choices.label: A. Add Personal Vulnerability
choices.description: Share a real fear or failure within your story. Risky but deeply authentic.
choices.feedback: Vulnerability is the most powerful tool in a storyteller's kit. Audiences connect to real struggle.

skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.resilience: Choosing to persist when things get hard develops resilience.

choices.label: B. Sensory Immersion
choices.description: Add vivid sensory details — smells, textures, sounds — that put the audience inside the story.
choices.feedback: Sensory detail transports listeners. When they can smell and feel your story, they live it.

skill_explanation.creativity: Exploring an unconventional approach shows creative thinking.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.

choices.label: C. Master the Power of Silence
choices.description: Learn to use pauses and silence for emotional impact. Less is more.
choices.feedback: Silence is terrifying on stage — and devastatingly powerful. A well-timed pause can say everything.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Resisting the quick fix in favor of lasting results shows maturity.

choices.label: D. Add Musical Elements
choices.description: Weave rhythm, song, or sound effects into your storytelling. Unconventional but memorable.
choices.feedback: Music in storytelling is bold and ancient. Bards have been doing it for millennia. You're in good company.

skill_explanation.creativity: Looking at the problem from a new angle demonstrates creativity.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Evaluating risk vs. reward is a key life skill.

rounds.situation: The competition website is publishing contestant profiles this week. Coach Maya says this is your chance to build a 'storyteller brand' — a consistent identity that judges and audiences remember. How do you want to be known?
rounds.goal: Craft your public identity as a storyteller.
rounds.coaching_moment: Strategic thinking: A personal brand isn't about being fake — it's about being intentionally, consistently YOU. What do you want people to remember?
rounds.reflection_prompt: How is building a personal brand different from just being yourself? Is it more honest or less?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager designing their competition profile on a laptop, creative mood board on wall, storytelling competition branding materials, focused creative work

choices.label: A. The Authentic Voice
choices.description: Brand yourself as raw, honest, and unfiltered. 'The storyteller who tells it like it is.'
choices.feedback: Authenticity is the rarest brand. In a world of polished performances, raw truth stands out.

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.

choices.label: B. The Creative Innovator
choices.description: Position yourself as the one who breaks conventions. 'Storytelling reimagined.'
choices.feedback: The innovator brand is exciting but risky. Judges either love it or dismiss it. Fortune favors the bold.

skill_explanation.creativity: Combining ideas in unexpected ways shows innovative thinking.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Taking a calculated risk shows you can handle uncertainty.

choices.label: C. The Community Storyteller
choices.description: Frame yourself as someone who tells stories for the community, not just for competition.
choices.feedback: Community-focused storytelling has deep roots. When you serve the audience, they champion you.

skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.

choices.label: D. The Scholar Performer
choices.description: Emphasize technique, research, and mastery. 'A student of the craft.'
choices.feedback: The scholar brand impresses judges who value craft. Your preparation becomes your superpower.

skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Waiting for the right moment instead of rushing shows self-control.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.

rounds.situation: The first preliminary round is next week. You're hit with a wave of stage fright — sweaty palms, racing thoughts, and the urge to quit. Coach Maya says this is normal, but how you handle it defines your trajectory.
rounds.goal: Develop a strategy to manage performance anxiety.
rounds.coaching_moment: Resilience: Stage fright isn't weakness — it's your brain preparing for something important. The goal isn't to eliminate fear, but to perform through it.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Is nervousness a sign that something matters to you? How can fear become fuel?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Nervous teenager backstage before a performance, deep breathing, hands shaking, supportive mentor nearby, spotlight visible through curtain, dramatic lighting

choices.label: A. Breathing & Mindfulness
choices.description: Learn box breathing and visualization techniques. Calm the body, calm the mind.
choices.feedback: Breathing techniques are used by Navy SEALs and Olympic athletes. Your body can teach your mind to be calm.

skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.

choices.label: B. Exposure Therapy: Perform Everywhere
choices.description: Force yourself to perform in uncomfortable places — bus stops, cafeterias, family gatherings.
choices.feedback: The best way to beat fear is to face it repeatedly. Every awkward performance makes the real one easier.

skill_explanation.resilience: Facing challenges head-on strengthens your resilience over time.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.

choices.label: C. Create a Pre-Performance Ritual
choices.description: Develop a specific routine — music, stretches, a lucky phrase — to enter 'performance mode.'
choices.feedback: Rituals create consistency. When everything else is uncertain, your routine is an anchor.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Prioritizing long-term gains over short-term comfort builds character.

choices.label: D. Reframe: Fear as Excitement
choices.description: Use cognitive reframing — tell yourself 'I'm excited' instead of 'I'm scared.' Same physiology, different story.
choices.feedback: Reframing is neuroscience in action. Your brain can't tell the difference between fear and excitement — you choose the label.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.
skill_explanation.creativity: Not settling for the obvious solution builds creative problem-solving.

rounds.situation: It's time. The preliminary round of the championship is here. Thirty contestants. Ten will advance. You have 7 minutes on stage. The judges are watching. The audience is packed. What's your performance strategy?
rounds.goal: Deliver your best performance in the preliminary round.
rounds.coaching_moment: Adaptability under pressure: Competition day tests everything — preparation, confidence, adaptability. The best performers adjust in real time.
rounds.reflection_prompt: When the stakes are highest, do you play it safe or take risks? Why?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager on stage at a storytelling competition, bright spotlight, packed audience, judges panel with clipboards, competition banner, dramatic atmosphere

choices.label: A. Play It Safe — Polished & Practiced
choices.description: Deliver exactly what you rehearsed. No improvisation, no surprises. Reliable and clean.
choices.feedback: A polished performance is respectable. The judges nod approvingly — but did it make them feel anything?

skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Choosing a future benefit over an immediate reward shows patience.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.

choices.label: B. Read the Room & Improvise
choices.description: Adapt your performance based on the audience's energy. Risky but electrifying when it works.
choices.feedback: Improvisation on stage is a high-wire act! The audience feels the alive energy, and the judges notice the bravery.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.

choices.label: C. Go Deep — Full Emotional Commitment
choices.description: Pour everything into the emotional core. You might break down, but if you land it, it's unforgettable.
choices.feedback: Raw emotional storytelling left the audience in stunned silence. Some judges had tears. That's power.

skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.
skill_explanation.resilience: Pushing through difficulty builds mental strength.

choices.label: D. Go Big — Theatrical Spectacle
choices.description: Use props, movement, and character voices. High energy, high entertainment value.
choices.feedback: The audience was on the edge of their seats! Theatrical storytelling is unforgettable — love it or hate it, nobody ignores it.

skill_explanation.creativity: Thinking outside the box leads to more original solutions.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Not always playing it safe helps you grow as a decision-maker.

rounds.situation: You advanced to the semifinals! But the judges' feedback was mixed — praise for some elements, sharp criticism for others. Coach Maya says how you respond to feedback this week determines whether you grow or crumble.
rounds.goal: Decide how to process and respond to competition feedback.
rounds.coaching_moment: Resilience and growth mindset: Feedback is a mirror, not a verdict. The best storytellers use criticism as fuel for growth.
rounds.reflection_prompt: How do you separate useful feedback from opinions that don't serve your vision?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager reading judges' scorecard with mixed emotions, coach pointing at areas for improvement, rehearsal room with notes on whiteboard, determined expression

choices.label: A. Major Overhaul Based on Feedback
choices.description: Rewrite significant portions of your story to address every critique. Responsive but risky.
choices.feedback: Massive rewrites show humility but can destroy what made your story unique. Be careful not to lose your voice.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.
skill_explanation.resilience: Choosing to persist when things get hard develops resilience.

choices.label: B. Surgical Fixes Only
choices.description: Address the valid criticisms while protecting your core story. Strategic and measured.
choices.feedback: Smart editing. You fixed what needed fixing and protected what was working. That's creative maturity.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Investing effort now for later payoff builds discipline.

choices.label: C. Ignore Critics & Double Down
choices.description: Trust your original vision and make it BIGGER. Bold but might alienate judges.
choices.feedback: Conviction is admirable. Some of the greatest art was made by people who ignored the critics — but some of the worst was too.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Evaluating risk vs. reward is a key life skill.
skill_explanation.creativity: Exploring an unconventional approach shows creative thinking.

choices.label: D. Seek Peer Collaboration
choices.description: Bring in trusted friends to workshop the story together. Fresh eyes, shared ownership.
choices.feedback: Collaboration brings perspectives you'd never find alone. Your story gains richness from other lived experiences.

skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.

rounds.situation: The semifinal has a twist — you must pitch your story to the judges before performing it. In 2 minutes, convince them why YOUR story deserves to win. Coach Maya says this is where brand narrative meets persuasion.
rounds.goal: Craft a compelling pitch for why your story matters.
rounds.coaching_moment: Communication and persuasion: Pitching is storytelling about your storytelling. It requires clarity, confidence, and conviction.
rounds.reflection_prompt: How is persuading someone different from entertaining them? Can you do both at once?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager confidently pitching to a judges panel, gesturing while speaking, presentation notes in hand, semifinal competition setting, spotlit podium

choices.label: A. Evidence-Based Pitch
choices.description: Research your story's themes and back your pitch with real data and references. Intellectual and credible.
choices.feedback: Data gives your story gravitas. The judges see you as not just a performer but a thinker.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Resisting the quick fix in favor of lasting results shows maturity.

choices.label: B. Pitch Through a Mini-Story
choices.description: Pitch your story by telling a tiny version of it. Meta, clever, and memorable.
choices.feedback: A pitch that IS a story? Brilliant. Judges love recursion — it shows you live and breathe narrative.

skill_explanation.creativity: Looking at the problem from a new angle demonstrates creativity.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.

choices.label: C. Raw Passion Pitch
choices.description: Speak from the heart about why this story matters to you personally. Vulnerable and fiery.
choices.feedback: Passion is contagious. When you genuinely care, the judges feel it. Authenticity trumps polish every time.

skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.

choices.label: D. Audience Testimonials
choices.description: Share quotes and reactions from people who've heard your story. Let the audience speak for you.
choices.feedback: Social proof is powerful persuasion. When judges hear that real people were moved, they take notice.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.
skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.

rounds.situation: You made the finals! Five storytellers remain. The championship is next week. Coach Maya says this final week of preparation is about refining, not reinventing. But the temptation to make big changes is strong.
rounds.goal: Make your final preparation decisions before the championship.
rounds.coaching_moment: Delayed gratification: At this stage, restraint is power. The urge to change everything is strong, but trust the work you've done.
rounds.reflection_prompt: When is it wisdom to stop changing and trust your preparation?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager in intense final rehearsal, empty auditorium, single spotlight, notes and scripts neatly organized, determination on face, championship banner visible

choices.label: A. Polish Every Detail
choices.description: Micro-rehearse every pause, gesture, and word. Pursue perfection.
choices.feedback: Perfection in preparation breeds confidence on stage. Every tiny detail has been considered.

skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Waiting for the right moment instead of rushing shows self-control.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.

choices.label: B. Add a Wildcard Element
choices.description: Introduce one unexpected twist — a surprise ending, an audience interaction, a prop nobody expects.
choices.feedback: A wildcard in the finals? Either genius or disaster. But nobody ever won a championship by being forgettable.

skill_explanation.creativity: Combining ideas in unexpected ways shows innovative thinking.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Taking a calculated risk shows you can handle uncertainty.

choices.label: C. Rest & Mental Reset
choices.description: Take a day off. Let your subconscious process. Come to the finals fresh, not exhausted.
choices.feedback: Strategic rest is an elite skill. Freshness on competition day is worth more than one extra rehearsal.

skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.

choices.label: D. Intensive Mentor Session
choices.description: Spend the entire day with Coach Maya for a deep one-on-one session. Extract every last insight.
choices.feedback: An intensive mentor session at this stage is like a final tune-up before a race. Coach Maya pushes you to your absolute best.

skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Prioritizing long-term gains over short-term comfort builds character.
skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.

rounds.situation: This is it. The Regional Storytelling Championship finals. Five finalists. One stage. Three judges. 500 people in the audience. The lights dim, your name is called. How do you perform the story of your life?
rounds.coaching_moment: Integration: Everything you've built — narrative, voice, presence, emotion, brand — comes together in this one moment. Trust yourself.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What have you learned about yourself as a storyteller? What will you carry forward regardless of the result?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager on championship stage, full spotlight, packed 500-person auditorium, judges panel front row, competition trophy visible, emotional peak performance moment

choices.label: A. The Masterpiece — Full Technical Brilliance
choices.description: Execute everything perfectly. Every technique, every beat, every nuance — flawless.
choices.feedback: Technical brilliance at its finest. The judges are impressed by your mastery. A performance built on weeks of dedicated craft.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Choosing a future benefit over an immediate reward shows patience.

choices.label: B. The Heart — Pure Emotional Truth
choices.description: Forget technique. Tell it from the heart. Let the audience see the real you.
choices.feedback: You stripped away all artifice and gave the audience something real. Some people are crying. That's storytelling at its most human.

skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.
skill_explanation.resilience: Facing challenges head-on strengthens your resilience over time.

choices.label: C. The Revolution — Break Every Rule
choices.description: Do something nobody has ever done on this stage. Walk into the audience. Change the ending live. Make them gasp.
choices.feedback: You just redefined what storytelling can be. The audience is on their feet. Some judges look stunned. Others are writing furiously. History remembers the rule-breakers.

skill_explanation.creativity: Not settling for the obvious solution builds creative problem-solving.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.

choices.label: D. The Connection — Make It About Them
choices.description: Turn your performance into a shared experience. Ask the audience a question. Make eye contact. Include them.
choices.feedback: You made 500 strangers feel like they were part of your story. That's not just storytelling — that's magic.

skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.

rounds.situation: Judge Stern has publicly flagged your entry as 'at risk of disqualification' due to low quality in preliminary reviews. The news spreads fast — other contestants smirk, and your confidence takes a massive hit. Coach Maya says you have one week to prove yourself or face elimination before the semifinals even begin.
rounds.goal: Respond to the rejection warning and save your championship run.
rounds.coaching_moment: Resilience under pressure: Rejection is not the end — it's information. How you respond reveals your true character as a storyteller.
rounds.reflection_prompt: When someone in authority dismisses your work, how do you decide whether to change or stand firm?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager backstage looking at a 'disqualification warning' notice, disappointed expression, crumpled papers, coach offering support in background, dramatic shadows

choices.label: A. Emergency Story Rewrite
choices.description: Pull an all-nighter and completely rewrite your weakest sections to address the judges' concerns.
choices.feedback: A frantic rewrite under pressure. You addressed the critics, but at what cost to your voice?

skill_explanation.resilience: Pushing through difficulty builds mental strength.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.

choices.label: B. Request a Private Re-Audition
choices.description: Ask Judge Stern for a 5-minute private performance. Show them what you can really do.
choices.feedback: Bold move! A private audition is a high-stakes gamble. Judge Stern is tough but fair — and you showed courage.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.

choices.label: C. Rally Community Support
choices.description: Organize a free storytelling session in your neighborhood. Build grassroots audience love that even judges can't ignore.
choices.feedback: Grassroots support! When the community rallies behind you, the judges notice. Storytelling belongs to the people.

skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.creativity: Thinking outside the box leads to more original solutions.

choices.label: D. Accept the Criticism & Focus on Growth
choices.description: Acknowledge the weakness publicly, thank the judge, and commit to visible improvement. Humility as strategy.
choices.feedback: Humility under fire is rare and powerful. Judge Stern respects your maturity. Real growth begins with honest self-assessment.

skill_explanation.resilience: Choosing to persist when things get hard develops resilience.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Investing effort now for later payoff builds discipline.

rounds.situation: Rival Rai's experimental storytelling went viral, and suddenly your approach feels stale. You sit down to rehearse and... nothing. The words won't come. Your mind is blank. The creative well has run dry. Coach Maya says creative blocks happen to every artist — but the competition won't wait.
rounds.goal: Break through the creative block before it derails your championship bid.
rounds.coaching_moment: Creativity under pressure: Creative blocks are not about talent — they're about fear. Break the pattern, change the environment, trust the process.
rounds.reflection_prompt: When your creativity feels stuck, what helps you get unstuck? Is pressure the enemy of creativity, or can it be a catalyst?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Teenager staring at blank page in frustration, crumpled papers around desk, phone showing rival's viral video, clock ticking on wall, moody dramatic lighting

choices.label: A. Unplug & Go Into Nature
choices.description: Leave everything behind. Walk in a park, sit by a river, listen to the world. Let inspiration find you.
choices.feedback: Nature reboots the creative brain. Studies show walking increases creative output by 60%. You return with fresh eyes.

skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.

choices.label: B. Study the Masters
choices.description: Watch recordings of legendary storytellers. Let their craft inspire yours — don't copy, but learn.
choices.feedback: Good artists borrow, great artists steal wisely. Studying masters fills your creative reservoir with new possibilities.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.
skill_explanation.creativity: Exploring an unconventional approach shows creative thinking.

choices.label: C. Stream-of-Consciousness Freewrite
choices.description: Set a timer for 30 minutes and write without stopping. No editing, no judgment. Just let it flow.
choices.feedback: Freewriting bypasses your inner critic. In the mess of unfiltered words, there are always gems waiting to be found.

skill_explanation.creativity: Looking at the problem from a new angle demonstrates creativity.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Not always playing it safe helps you grow as a decision-maker.

choices.label: D. Creative Jam Session
choices.description: Invite friends for an improv storytelling session. Let play and laughter break the block.
choices.feedback: Collaboration and play are creativity's best friends. Laughter loosens the brain. New ideas emerge from shared energy.

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.

glossary_terms.definition: The structure of a story from beginning through conflict to resolution — the backbone of compelling storytelling.
The distinctive personality and style that makes a storyteller's work recognizable and consistent across different pieces.
The ability to command attention and fill a performance space with energy, confidence, and charisma.
The quality of a story that makes the audience feel genuine emotions and connect personally with the narrative.
Using narrative techniques to influence an audience's beliefs, feelings, or actions — storytelling with a purpose beyond entertainment.
A psychological technique of changing how you interpret a situation — for example, relabeling stage fright as excitement.
A period when a creative person feels unable to produce new work or ideas, often caused by fear, perfectionism, or burnout.
The skill of modifying your message, tone, and delivery to suit different listeners while maintaining your core story.

endings.title: Master Storyteller
endings.message: Your narrative craft was extraordinary. Every sentence was sculpted, every scene perfectly paced. The judges awarded you the championship title for sheer storytelling excellence. Coach Maya wipes a tear — you've surpassed even her expectations. Your story will be published in the National Young Writers' Anthology. Your legacy: a storyteller who proved that craft is the ultimate superpower.

endings.title: Audience Captivator
endings.message: The audience voted you their favorite by a landslide! Your performance had 500 people laughing, crying, and cheering. The 'People's Choice Award' is yours. Event organizers invite you to tour schools across the region. Your legacy: a storyteller who understood that stories belong to the audience, not the teller.

endings.title: Creative Original
endings.message: The 'Most Original Performance' award goes to YOU! Your bold creative choices left the judges arguing — some loved it, some were puzzled, but nobody was indifferent. A literary magazine features your work. Even Rival Rai gives you a genuine handshake. Your legacy: a storyteller who dared to be different when everyone else played safe.

endings.title: Stage Commander
endings.message: Your stage presence was undeniable. From the moment you stepped into the spotlight, every eye was locked on you. The judges gave you the 'Best Performance' award. Drama schools reach out with scholarship offers. Coach Maya says she hasn't seen this kind of natural command since she was competing. Your legacy: a performer who owned every second on stage.

endings.title: Emerging Voice
endings.message: You didn't win the championship, but something more important happened — you found your voice. The experience of crafting a story, facing your fears, and performing on a real stage has changed you. Coach Maya smiles: 'This was never about the trophy. It was about discovering who you are as a storyteller.' Next year, you'll be back. Stronger. Your legacy: a storyteller in the making, just getting started.
